pr_body:
In a mixed 6.x and 7.x cluster, a search that uses dfs_query_then_fetch can cause a transport serialization errors. 

This is related to https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/LUCENE-8007, which was introduced in Lucene 8 and adds stricter checks to TermStatistics and CollectionStatistics, and https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/LUCENE-8020, which was introduced in Lucene 8 and avoids bogus term stats (e.g. docfreq=0). 

Co-authored-by: Julie Tibshirani <julietibs@gmail.com>

Closes #75349
pr_title: Fix term stats when talking to ES 6

review_comment: It'd be great to add a comment here explaining why this backwards compatibility logic is needed. I also wonder if it's worth factoring out a common method like `readSingleTermStats` to use in both `AggregatedDfs` and `DfsSearchResult`?

> I also wonder if it's worth factoring out a common method like readSingleTermStats to use in both AggregatedDfs and DfsSearchResult

These methods are similar, but not quite the same. I'm therefore inclined to keep them separate.

> It'd be great to add a comment here explaining why this backwards compatibility logic is needed.

I have added docs to that effect in 0aa3cf78f08.

Lucene seems to be doing it the other way arround: `if (docCount == -1) { docCount = maxDoc; }` reading https://github.com/apache/lucene-solr/blob/releases/lucene-solr/7.7.3/lucene/core/src/java/org/apache/lucene/search/similarities/BM25Similarity.java#L99.
Makes sense. I'm mainly wondering how to exercise this logic (I can't see a way for this to happen with the codecs that we offer).
Right, the default codec would always return a non-negative docCount. Maybe one approach would be to have this case only covered through a unit test that emulates 6.x serialization logic.
I've added a unit test in 5abe7d351d9. Not sure it adds much though.
